neighbours.label: a word marking gradual, ongoing change over time (increasing, progressive, steadily, ever-expanding, rising), as against the same topics stated as a fixed amount or a sudden one-off change
fire: In recent years farmers have faced increasing costs for fuel and seed.
The patient showed progressive weakening of the eyesight over a decade.
Sales of electric bikes have climbed steadily since the subsidy began.
The city is ever-expanding, swallowing the villages around it.
Sea levels keep rising, a few millimetres every year.
Teachers report an increasing number of pupils who struggle to read.
Glaciers in the valley have been steadily shrinking for a century.
The illness brings progressive stiffness in the joints as people age.
quiet: In recent years farmers have paid about forty dollars for a bag of seed.
The patient showed sudden blurring of the eyesight one morning.
Sales of electric bikes reached five thousand units last year.
The city is large and has several villages around it.
The sea level at the pier is two metres at high tide.
Teachers report that twelve pupils in the class struggle to read.
Glaciers in the valley collapsed in a single night of storms.
The illness brings stiffness in the joints after a long walk.
